original_value: Small object detection is an interesting topic in computer vision. With the rapid development in deep learning, it has drawn attention of several researchers with innovations in approaches to join a race. These innovations proposed comprise region proposals, divided grid cell, multiscale feature maps, and new loss function. As a result, performance of object detection has recently had significant improvements. However, most of the state-of-the-art detectors, both in one-stage and two-stage approaches, have struggled with detecting small objects. In this study, we evaluate current state-of-the-art models based on deep learning in both approaches such as Fast RCNN, Faster RCNN, RetinaNet, and YOLOv3. We provide a profound assessment of the advantages and limitations of models. Specifically, we run models with different backbones on different datasets with multiscale objects to find out what types of objects are suitable for each model along with backbones. Extensive empirical evaluation was conducted on 2 standard datasets, namely, a small object dataset and a filtered dataset from PASCAL VOC 2007. Finally, comparative results and analyses are then presented.

result.paraphrase: Small object detection is a compelling topic in computer vision. With the rapid progress of deep learning, it has attracted several researchers, leading to a race of innovations in detection methods. These proposed innovations include region proposals, divided grid cells, multiscale feature maps, and new loss functions. As a result, object detection performance has improved significantly in recent years. However, most state-of-the-art detectors, in both one-stage and two-stage frameworks, still struggle to detect small objects. In this study, we assess current deep learning-based state-of-the-art models in both approaches, including Fast RCNN, Faster RCNN, RetinaNet, and YOLOv3. We offer a thorough evaluation of the strengths and weaknesses of these models. In particular, we test models with different backbones on different datasets containing multiscale objects to determine which object types are best suited to each model and backbone. Extensive empirical evaluation was carried out on two standard datasets: a small object dataset and a filtered dataset from PASCAL VOC 2007. Finally, comparative results and analyses are presented.
